Q: The Dir() function vs. referencing another VBA project A:

Dir's search state is per VBA project. This means foo calling Dir("C:\") doesn't create a search context inside the project where bar lives. When bar calls Dir() without an argument, it has no active search to continue, so it throws Run-time error '5': Invalid procedure call or argument.

The Dir function has to start with a pathname in the local project before you can use the no-argument version.

Try this:

Sub bar()
    Debug.Print Dir("C:\")
End Sub

But if you need to share a single file cursor across project boundaries, Dir isn't the right tool. I'd use FileSystemObject instead, or just keep the entire loop logic inside foo so the state doesn't get lost.

Q: SOLVED Common Lisp Reader Macro Conflict A:

While trying to get some more info for @Shawn, I stumbled across the answer. If I load the packages as :cl-schedule then :clache (even just those two in the REPL), I get the macro error. If I load them in the reverse order, everything's fine. I update my system definition to be this:

(asdf:defsystem "-----"
  :version "0.0.1"
  :author "-----"
  :license "MIT"
  :depends-on (:alpaca-api
               :named-readtables
               :ls-xsd
               :clache
               :cl-schedule
               :str
               :alexandria)
  :components ((:module "src"
                :components
                ((:file "utils")
                 (:file "main"))))
  :description ""
  :in-order-to ((test-op (test-op "-----/tests"))))

reversing the order of :clache and :cl-schedule. This solved all the problems, and the system loaded just fine.

Thanks guys!

P.S. Is anyone willing/able to enlighten me as to why the order of dependencies can cause an error like this one? Thanks.
